newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Miami air cargo rates to Central America jump.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Miami air cargo rates to Central America jump.

text.p: Air cargo rates ex Miami are increasing with big jumps coming in rates to Central America, a Reuters survey of cargo carriers, freight forwarders, sales agents and others shows.
Rates to Central America have risen sharply since the beginning of the year, forwarders said.
One general sales agent said, for example, that rates from Miami to Costa Rica have risen from 38 cents per kilo at year- end to as much as 60 cents per kilo currently.
"These market are never very stable," an executive for one Central American carrier said. "But we don't expect rates to go up much more than this," he said.
The air carrier blamed the higher rates on more expensive fuel, bigger security bills and other costs.
Rate edged up a little to South America. For example, rates ex Miami to Santiago are up from $1.72 per kilo at the last survey to $1.85 per kilo currently.

Chile exports mostly perishables to the United States and the rest of the world through Miami International Airport. One big export is fish, especially salmon. Chile also exports a lot of fruits and is in the middle of the season for stone frutis such as peaches.
Forwarders complained that the bargain basement rates they have gotten in past years during Valentine's Day to flower producing countries such as Colombia and Ecuador were not offered this year.
They get the cheap rates because there is a great deal of capacity added to carry the Valentines flowers north to Miami and the planes fly south with little freight.
"There were no great deals this year," said one forwarder.

European carriers are rasing their rates ex-Miami to Europe effective in March and April, forwarders said. One forwarder pegged the increases ex-MIA to Europe average about 8 percent to 10 percent depending on route and carrier.
For example, Air France has raised rates ex-Miami about 5 percent depanding on the route, executives said.
Freight ex-Miami to Europe is very heavy, forwarders said.
"Space is very tight," said one forwarder.
One European airline said every one of their flights is full of cargo.
All the forwarders and air carriers said business right now through Miami is strong to and from most destinations.
Carriers have seen a flurry of air exports to Bolivia. Challenge Air Cargo has added one weekly flight to its current two and Arrow Air Inc. is considering starting a service.
"There is a lot of activity there right now," Jon Batchelor, president of Arrow said of Bolivia.

Like many Latin American countries, Bolivia is in the midst of putting some previously state-owned businesses in private hands, executives said. This creates a lot of exports to Brazil as the new owners modernize and upgrade the companies.
Rates to Bolivia are running about $2.00 per kilo.
The threatened strike by American Airlines pilots that lasted only a few minutes Feb. 15 disrupted cargo prior to the event and offered bargain rates for a few weeks after.
"We saw some rates of 50 percent off on some routes," said one executive from a competing all-cargo line.
The pilots are in a government-mandated 60-day negotiating period, so the same strike threat looms again in mid-April. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
